recipes.name: Fresh Tomato Chili Sauce
ingredients_raw: 35 fresh tomatoes, peeled, seeded and chopped
4 red bell peppers, seeded and diced
0.33333334326744 cup fresh lime juice, or amount to taste
3 fresh hot chile peppers, seeded and chopped
1 tablespoon salt, or amount to taste

steps.text: Place tomatoes in a large pot over medium heat; simmer for 1 hour, skimming off any excess liquid or foam as necessary.

Stir bell peppers, vinegar, onion, white sugar, brown sugar, lime juice, chile peppers, and salt into tomatoes. Reduce heat to low; simmer until liquid reduces and sauce thickens, 3 to 5 hours more. Taste; adjust seasonings.

Meanwhile, inspect four 1-quart jars for cracks and rings for rust, discarding any defective ones. Immerse in simmering water until sauce is ready. Wash new, unused lids and rings in warm, soapy water.

Off heat, skim off any foam from sauce. Pack into the hot, sterilized jars, filling to within ¼ inch of tops. Run a clean knife or thin spatula around insides of jars to remove any air bubbles. Wipe rims with a moist paper towel to remove any residue. Top with lids and screw rings on tightly.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with water. Bring to a boil and lower jars 2 inches apart into boiling water using a holder. Pour in more boiling water to cover jars by at least 1 inch. Bring to a rolling boil, cover, and process for 10 minutes.

Remove jars from the stockpot; rest, several inches apart, 12 to 24 hours. Press centers of lids with a finger to ensure lids do not move up or down. Remove rings for storage and store in a cool, dark area.

raw_recipe.headline: Fresh Tomato Chili Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Richly flavored chili tomato sauce is easy with this old family recipe made with garden-fresh tomatoes, bell peppers, onions, lime juice, and sugar.

review.reviewBody: this is the best,one change i did was added celery other then that is is very good the longer it sits the better it will get thks Diane

This is a sweet and spicy recipe. I like it but need ideas on how to use it in other recipes. I used 1/4 Tsp crushed red peppers because I didn't have any hot peppers. Plenty of heat for me. I basically cut the recipe in half and made it a bit healthier by using Stevia & Sea salt. Very tasty recipe.

I still have my mother and grandmother's similar recipe for an English-style chili sauce that wasn't spicy. It calls for: a peck of tomatoes (12-15 lbs.), peeled and cut fine; 2 quarts of onions (measured, I suspect, after peeling and quartering) ground in a (manual) meat grinder; 6 red or green bell peppers, also ground; 4 cups brown sugar; 4 tsp. salt; 3 heaping tsp. ground cinnamon; 1½ tsp. ground nutmeg; ½ box mixed whole spice (which would be about half of a 1.5 ounce jar of today's McCormick pickling spice) tied into cheesecloth; 1 scant tsp. ground black pepper; 1 cup cider vinegar. Cook 3 hours, very slowly, stirring often. To be canned in sterile jars. The end of August or early September is the recommended season (tomato season in the northern U.S.). Were I to make it these days, I think I'd reduce the brown sugar to 1 cup, and grind some seeded jalapenos and/or serranos into the mix. (I laugh now at the "scant tsp." of black pepper. So timid!)

Hi team. I made this yesterday. All at a bit of a guess as “35 tomatoes” is a little hard to represent in a weight, so I used what I had and basically halved all other ingredients except the chilli, I used a few more but they were wildfire chillies, about 77grams of them to the 1400 grams of tomatoes, anyway all other ingredients were halved and also, I also blended it with a stick blender after about an hour and a half of the final simmering. turned out great, A bit of a sweet taste hits the tongue at first, then the zing, Also added Coriander and basil, and switched the lime juice for lemon juice, just cause I had it. Hope this helps someone else who isn’t sure of the 35 tomatoes weight wise.
I didn't add any sugar at all, still come very good and sweet.

My wife and I have fallen in love with this sauce. So far, we have used it on pierogis and chip dip. Due to health concerns and personal taste preferences, we have reduced the sugar by half. This is a multi-purpose sauce, and I plan on making a lot this year. Thank you, Janet, for sharing.

Frost came early. What to do with a bazillion pulled tomatoes? So I made three gallons of juice and reserved a gallon for chili sauce. Followed recipe close but cut sugar in half. It still had plenty of sweet. Kind of knocks your head back like Frank's sauce but much better. Cooked for some hours to reduce. A gallon seems a good amount to start as I had no idea how much 35 tomatoes was. Besides all my tomatoes were different sizes and types.
This is a great recipe, I finely chopped the peppers and onion and added celerly. Very much like an old family recipe I used years ago.

Just finished making the Chili Sauce. I had been looking for this for a few years and so happy to have found this one. I's sure the recipe is fabulous as is, but because I didn't have all ingredients this called for, I made a few substitutions. I didn't have fresh tomatoes so I used 10 reg. cans of diced tomatoes. I used 1/2 teas. ground cayenne pepper instead of the fresh chili peppers and added a couple of shakes of chili powder. Last but not least I only had 1 red bell pepper on hand so added green peppers. When almost ready to finish cooking I noticed that it wasn't as thick as I wanted so added 2 cans of tomato paste. I have it in the caner right now, but did a taste test before. It is delish!! Thanks so much Jan for this recipe. Next year I hope to make it from scratch. :) However, this was really easy. I ended up with 7 pints of sauce.
This is so sweet and all I can taste and smell is apple cider vinegar. I used Braggs, is that why? I don’t think it’s edible and I spent all day making it. I’m super bummed out!

First batch, I followed recipe exactly. Second batch split between 1 cup ACV and 1 cup distilled white. Also added half tsp of Chinese 5 spice. First batch getting ready to go in the canner now. Will let you know.
Turned out amazing, I made one batch to see how it turned out. Was delicious so I made 4 additional batches....
Sounds very good. You should post a lesser yielding recipe. 8 pints of sauce is too much for one family.
This was delicious. I used it to make sloppy joe's and my husband loved it. It canned nicely also!
It came out great/ a keeper. I don’t need a lot so only made a half batch.

We had excess tomatoes and sweet not so hot chilies (almost like small capsicum in flavour) from our garden. Found this recipe and it is amazing! Ours is not so hot as we didn’t add anything but our home grown chilies or rather capsicums (peppers) but it has an amazing fresh concentrated flavour of the tomatoes and chilies! Definitely will make it again.

I returned from a vacation to a garden full of ripe tomatoes and wanted to do something different with them. Based on reviews, I tried this Fresh Tomato Chili Sauce. I followed the recipe exactly. Not sure what I expected, but I find it oddly sweet. I am eager to try it in a recipe (meatloaf or chili soup) to see how it is when combined with other ingredients. My husband loves it! Once I've had a chance to try it in a recipe, I will edit my review.
